headline_marked: Student [[arrested in Gazipur for mocking Prime Minister]] and govt officials
headline: Student arrested in Gazipur for mocking Prime Minister and govt officials
summary: Sifat Abdullah, a 20-year-old Adamjee Cantonment College student, was detained by police following social media posts and a video criticizing the government.
details: Police in Gazipur have arrested 20-year-old Sifat Abdullah, a student of Adamjee Cantonment College, for allegedly making derogatory remarks about the Prime Minister, Tarique Rahman, and other government-affiliated individuals on social media.

The arrest took place around 8:30 PM on Thursday night in the Gacha area of Gazipur city. Gacha Police Station's Officer-in-Charge (OC) Golam Rabbani confirmed the arrest on Friday morning, stating that a case has been filed against Sifat.

According to police and local sources, Sifat had been posting critical content on social media for some time. The arrest followed a video where he expressed frustration over high electricity bills, complaining that his home received additional charges of 4,000 to 5,000 BDT

Following the news of the arrest, members of the National Citizens' Party (NCP) gathered at the Gacha Police Station on Thursday night to demand his release. They remained at the station until after 2:00 AM on Friday.

Ali Nasser Khan, the chief organizer of the NCP's central executive committee, described Sifat as a supporter of the NCP and a fan of the Inkilab Manch, claiming the arrest was unnecessary. He warned the police commissioner that if the arrest is not addressed, the issue could become an international concern.

NCP leaders claim Sifat participated in the July movement and frequently criticized government irregularities, decisions, and issues regarding oil, gas, and electricity on social media, while also criticizing other political parties.

headline_marked: 13 injured as [[clash erupts over 45-taka tea bill]] in Natore
headline: 13 injured as clash erupts over 45-taka tea bill in Natore
summary: A dispute between a tea stall owner and a grocer over a small unpaid bill escalated into multiple violent clashes, leaving 13 people injured.
details: A dispute over a 45-taka tea bill led to clashes between two groups in Bagatipara, Natore, leaving 13 people injured.
The incident began on Thursday afternoon at Jayantipur Bazar when a tea stall owner, Shamim Hossain, and a grocer, Mostafa, argued over the unpaid bill, which eventually turned into a physical fight.
The conflict escalated as relatives and acquaintances of both parties joined in, leading to multiple rounds of clashes at the market.
The injured were taken to the Bagatipara Upazila Health Complex around 7:30 PM for treatment.
Violence broke out again at the hospital around 8:30 PM as the two groups engaged in further arguments and fighting.
Police from the Bagatipara Model Police Station and hospital authorities intervened to bring the situation under control.
OC Sumon Chandra Das stated that while several people were treated for injuries, no formal written complaints have been filed by either side so far.
Police confirmed that the situation is currently calm and legal action will be taken if a formal complaint is received.
